references.text: Describes Israel's victory over Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan, whose kingdoms are now given to Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
Moses recounts how the land taken from Sihon and Og was given to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
Refers to the victory over Sihon and Og, and that their land was given as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
Summarizes the kings Israel defeated on the east side of the Jordan, including Sihon and Og, whose territories were given to the two and a half tribes.
Describes the inheritance land of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan, including the former kingdoms of Sihon and Og.
Joshua sends the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh back to their inheritance east of the Jordan that Moses gave them.
The continuation of the text describing how the descendants of Manasseh took possession of areas in Gilead and Bashan.
Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh are adopted by Jacob, which explains why Manasseh is counted as a separate tribe.
